name: 18th-Century Royal Palace at Caserta with the Park, the Aqueduct of Vanvitelli, and the San Leucio Complex
description: Near Naples, in the Campania town of Caserta, this vast Bourbon royal palace was begun in the 1750s by Charles III to rival Versailles. Behind it, a park of fountains and cascades climbs into wooded hills. Nearby are a historic silk-making village at San Leucio and a 38-kilometre aqueduct, whose triple-tiered stone arches stride across a valley to feed the palace's waters.
